status: CHANGED since last audit — but change is COSMETIC ONLY (verified via git diff eec95e5 'preparation for V3')
purpose: PhlimboEA (V1), the original Linear-Depletion staking yield farm. Deployed on mainnet, now INACTIVE (all users migrated to V2). Retained for reference during V3 development; header comment states it is safe to delete after V3 ships.

changeSummary.behavioralDelta: NONE. The only diff vs. previously-audited V1 is: (1) a new header comment 'all users migrated to PhlimboV2 ... safe to delete this contract'; (2) `forge fmt` reformatting of event declarations, ternaries, and multi-line expressions. No logic, no signature, no storage-layout change.
changeSummary.verificationMethod: git log -p src/Phlimbo.sol — the single touching commit (eec95e5) contains only comment + whitespace/formatting hunks.

reentrancyUNGuarded: claim (inherit V1 design; no cross-fn reentry demonstrated, external token calls are the trusted phUSD/stable)
verifiedProperties.pauseMechanism: yes — pauser-only (no owner-direct pause, unlike V3)

localFindings.description: V1 retains the documented Linear-Depletion rate-recompute bug: rewardPerSecond is recomputed inside _updatePool on every user interaction, re-anchoring the depletion window (this is exactly what V2/V3 fix by moving the recompute out). Per project CLAUDE.md the contract is DEPLOYED-INACTIVE and DO NOT MODIFY; the header comment says it is safe to delete post-V3. This run introduces no behavioral change to V1. Carry as a QA/ledger reconciliation item (dead code retained; bug is pre-existing/known, not newly introduced).
localFindings.recommendation: Delete PhlimboEA from the repo after V3 ships as the header comment instructs; no code change to the deployed contract. Reconcile the V1 rate-recompute bug against the existing ledger rather than re-reporting.

interfaceAbstraction.note: Predecessor/reference contract — profiled lightly for interaction surface only, per task scope. Inactive on mainnet; not a live interaction counterparty for V3 (the migration path is V2->V3, not V1->V3).

externalEntryPoints.accessControl: none (recipient defaults to msg.sender; no migrator role in V1)

trustAssumptions: V1 is inactive; no users staked. It is not wired as a migrator counterparty for the V2->V3 path.
phUSD mint role on V1 should be revoked when the contract is retired (out-of-scope wiring concern; note for operational review).
suspiciousAreas_forTier2: Minimal — no behavioral change. Only interaction concern: if V1 still holds a live phUSD mint role while inactive, that is a standing privilege that should be revoked at retirement (operational/QA, not a V3 code issue).
